root_idea.summary: The root centers on two principal orientations: passing onward or through, and the contrary of sweetness, namely bitterness or unpleasantness.
root_idea.development: From passing comes the notion of a time or occasion that has elapsed; from bitterness and tightly twisted rope develop extensions involving hardship, strength, firmness, and resistance.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Canonical Form I verb citation form.
QAC identifies this occurrence as a verbal noun, distinct from the finite verb.
Plural مَرَّات is presented under its singular citation form مَرَّة.
Singular occurrence noun and citation form.
Distinct vocalized noun مِرَّة with the Quranic strength sense.

senses.definition: To pass, go by or beyond, proceed along or through, or go away.
senses.usage_conditions: The construction may describe movement past a place or object, passage over or along something, or proceeding with something; in 7:189 it describes moving about with a light burden.

senses.definition: To pass on from something with disregard; to turn away from it without attending to it.
senses.usage_conditions: A figurative use in which passing becomes withdrawal or deliberate avoidance, as in passing by vain speech or turning away after relief.

senses.definition: More bitter; more severe or grievous in its unpleasantness.
senses.usage_conditions: A comparative adjective, used in the Quranic expression وَأَمَرُّ to intensify the comparison of bitterness or harshness.
A verbal noun of مَرَّ, used for the movement or passage of something, including the Quranic description of the mountains passing like clouds.

senses.definition: A time, occasion, instance, or single occurrence.
senses.usage_conditions: Used adverbially or in counting repetitions; the plural مَرَّات denotes times or occasions, while forms such as مَرَّتَيْنِ mean twice.
In the Quranic expression ذُو مِرَّةٍ, it describes one endowed with great strength and sound bodily capability; the expression is applied to Gabriel.

senses.definition: Continuing, lasting, or proceeding in a uniform course.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expressions سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ and يَوْمُ نَحْسٍ مُسْتَمِرٍّ, it can describe something ongoing, lasting, or constant in its course.

senses.definition: Effective or potent in carrying through its effect.
senses.usage_conditions: An interpretation of مُسْتَمِرّ applied to the ill-fortune that accomplishes what it is charged or constrained to accomplish.
An alternative Quranic interpretation of سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ, emphasizing that the enchantment passes away without lasting effect.
An alternative interpretation of the Quranic expressions in which persistence or potency is understood figuratively as bitterness or harshness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To run or flow, of water; to pass along or blow, of wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical extension of passing movement to flowing water or moving air.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a period to pass over someone; for a calamity to befall someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional use with a person or object as the affected party.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be overcome by an attack of bile or gall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is used of a person whose bile becomes roused.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something bitter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II has an intensive or causative force relative to becoming bitter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pass, go by, or go away with another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III construction expressing passing in association with another party.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone or something pass, go away, or pass over or across.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV is causative; it can govern a person or object and can describe making something pass along a bridge or drawing an object across a surface.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To recite poetry fluently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To twist a rope or thread tightly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same twisting image is used figuratively of time or fortune as alternately untwisting and twisting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To struggle or strive with someone, twisting around him or his neck in an attempt to throw him down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or physical contest construction; the related reciprocal form is تَمَارَّا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become bitter; transitively, to make something bitter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is used both intransitively of food or another thing becoming bitter and transitively in the sense covered by مَرَّرَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiom, to refrain from saying or doing what is harmful or beneficial.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression مَا أَمَرَّ وَمَا أَحْلَى is explained as neither uttering a bitter or sweet saying nor causing harm or benefit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For two people to struggle or strive with one another, each twisting the other’s neck to throw him down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reciprocal Form VI usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To continue in one uniform course or state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical Form X use of a thing, affair, or process that continues regularly or constantly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become tightly twisted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used literally of a rope and figuratively of becoming firm or resistant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become strong, firm, resistant, or accustomed to something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative development from a tightly twisted rope; it can describe firmness against an opponent or habituation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For one’s condition to become sound after being bad or corrupt; to repent and become upright.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported figurative use concerning a person’s moral or practical state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become bitter, especially of food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X use synonymous with becoming bitter under أَمَرَّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To murmur or grumble; to be angry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A quadriliteral usage reported as an established meaning, with anger described as its likely primary sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make water pass or flow over the surface of the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use involving the movement of water across ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shake, quiver, or quake; to become smooth like marble; of sand, to move from side to side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meanings vary with the subject: body, flesh, marble-like surfaces, or sand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bitter; unpleasant to the taste.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also applied figuratively to a life or experience that is harsh or disagreeable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Myrrh, a bitter medicinal substance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A named medicine used in several traditional preparations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a figurative expression, afflictions or calamities that befall someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The phrase مَرَّتْ عَلَيْهِ أَمْزَارٌ uses the bitterness image for hardships.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Loathing or aversion of the mind or stomach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of a mind or stomach characterized as bitter, repelled, or disgusted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A surname of Iblis, literally associated with bitterness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper-name usage rather than an ordinary adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A time, one occasion, a single act, bout, or temporary occurrence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes adverbial expressions such as once, twice, at once, or repeatedly on different occasions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act or occurrence of passing, going by, or going away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of passing, distinct from the Quranic strength use of the same vocalized form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A firm twist or single strand of a rope.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun can denote a strong twisting or one individual twist in a rope.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intellect, sound judgment, firmness, or strength of mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of firmness; this Classical sense is distinct from the Quranic expression denoting strength.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bile or gall, one of the bodily humors.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote the yellow or black bile among the traditional four humors.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bitter or sour tree or herb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective plant name with a singular form in ـة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slender, long, strongly twisted rope, or a single strand of rope.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can describe a rope made of several strands or a strongly twisted individual strand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strong or powerfully made.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival use derived from the firmness of a tightly twisted rope.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Resolution, determination, or strength of mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use for firmness of character or purpose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bitterness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of quality, also extended figuratively to unpleasantness or aversion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Loathing or aversion of the mind or stomach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression for disgust or repugnance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The gallbladder, the organ containing bile.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun; the lexical evidence notes exceptions among certain animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seasoning or condiment eaten with food to make it savory.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A culinary noun, distinct from the adjective مُرّ meaning bitter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tall tree or cane from which spears are made; also a spear made from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is also associated morphologically with the root مرن.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Marble or a hard, clear kind of soft white stone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A stone noun, synonymous with or related to رُخَام.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft and quivering in the flesh; a soft, quivering body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a body or person whose flesh quivers when rising.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most tightly twisted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative adjective derived from the rope-twisting branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firmer or more faithful to a compact or agreement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative comparison based on firmness of twisting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two bitter or grievous hardships, such as poverty and decrepitude or disease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed figurative dual expression for severe adversity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pair of bitter plants, identified as aloe and mustard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional plant-name expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Calamities, evil, or a grievous and distressing experience.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed expression such as لَقِيتُ مِنْهُ الأَمَرَّيْنِ, literally experiencing the two bitter things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of passing or passage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun, also attested as a verbal noun in related usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rope, thread, or other thing tightly twisted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes something made firm by twisting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strongly or firmly made, of a man or horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival extension from tightly twisted material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Overcome by bile; a person whose bile is roused.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial adjective describing the condition caused by bile.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strong in altercation and not weary of laboring or striving.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed phrase describing persistence and endurance in contention or effort.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Constantly obtaining or unvarying, of a custom or practice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical active-participle use outside the Quranic expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spade or digging implement; also its handle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A supplemental technical noun for a tool used in cultivated soil or mud.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An anesthetic herb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant name in a supplemental lexical entry.
